scope: The eight files named as next by M39 (src/asn1/{t_pkey,t_spki,typ,x_bignum,x_info,x_int64,x_long,x_pkey}.rs). Contract checks against OpenSSL 3.6.4 for the two number printers, the SPKI printer, the generated d2i_*/i2d_* wrapper layer and ASN1_NULL sentinel, the BIGNUM/CBIGNUM primitive hooks, the LONG/ZLONG slot-resident primitives, the eight fixed-width integer primitives, and the X509_INFO/X509_PKEY lifecycles. Two inaccurate unsafe-contract statements repaired, both documentation-only with no behaviour change. No new unsafe operation, FFI symbol, allocator coordinate or repr(C) layout introduced.
worktree: source: src/asn1/t_spki.rs and src/asn1/x_int64.rs contract statements repaired; src/asn1/{t_pkey,typ,x_bignum,x_info,x_long,x_pkey}.rs audited with no source change. queue/receipt: REMAINING-AUDIT.txt, AUDITED-FILES.txt, PERFILE-INDEX.md section 44 and this file.

reconciliation.method: AUDITED-FILES.txt is the union of each mechanism sweep's structured .files array, the M1 files, the structured per-file records and each boundary sweep's structured boundaries. The eight files added here were the first eight entries of REMAINING-AUDIT.txt and were inserted at their alphabetical asn1-block positions (t_pkey/t_spki after string, typ after time, x_bignum/x_info/x_int64/x_long/x_pkey after x_algor).
reconciliation.difference_from_357: M39 left 357 audited / 406 unaudited. This batch moves the eight files it named as next; no skipped boundary was removed from the remaining queue.

mechanisms: BN_is_negative / BN_is_zero / BN_bn2bin and limb magnitude length
OwnedBuf::new_cleansed scratch for the wide-number magnitude
file_dispositions.note: The wide-number scratch is nbytes + 1 bytes with a leading zero for the sign pad; BN_bn2bin writes exactly nbytes at +1 and the buf[1] & 0x80 decision, formats, signs, widths and failure tails match t_pkey.c. The local owner is the authority's single cleansing free on both exits. A null number is not part of the stated contract and is never dereferenced in Rust.

The # Safety contract named only spkac, while the body also reads spkac->pubkey, spkac->challenge, sig_algor.algorithm and signature. The contract now names those mandatory template fields (the item descriptors make all five present on a valid value). No code change.

mechanisms: item_functions! generated d2i_*/i2d_* wrappers for string and multistring types
file_dispositions.note: Every wrapper is the authority's one-line forward through the shared item codec; a null value slot is handled by item_d2i, pp remains the caller's obligation, and the ASN1_NULL sentinel (ASN1_VALUE *)1 is returned and never dereferenced, matching tasn_typ.c. The stack wrappers cast the value-slot representation only and immediately hand it to the item layer.

bn_free reads BN_SENSITIVE from the item and takes BN_clear_free for CBIGNUM; a failed decode frees the value this call allocated and nulls the slot, matching x_bignum.c. The pad decision (BN_num_bits & 0x7), magnitude write and BN_FLG_CONSTTIME stamp match. No intermediate ASN1_STRING is built.

mechanisms: X509_INFO repr(C) layout and offset assertions
file_dispositions.note: _new is the authority's zero-allocation and _free releases certificate, CRL, private key and enc_data, then the record, each exactly once. The zeroed image is the authority's own constructed state, so the OB-3 zero-state sweep is sound.

mechanisms: eight fixed-width items with size used as a flags word
file_dispositions.note: A decoded UINT32 is allocated by uint64_new (eight bytes), which is the authority's own uint32_c2i choice, while prim_new allocates four bytes through uint32_new. uint32_free's SAFETY statement claimed the four-byte allocation unconditionally; it now states both provenances and that OwnedBlock's Drop releases the base pointer, which is extent-independent and frees the wider decode block whole. The arithmetic, truncation, ABS_INT32_MIN guard and error coordinates match x_int64.c. No code change.

mechanisms: long_i2c / long_c2i arithmetic and padding/sign rules
file_dispositions.note: The value lives in the ASN1_VALUE slot itself; reads and writes use read_unaligned/write_unaligned at the slot address, exactly the authority's memcpy. The negative encode is 0 - utmp - 1, padding/sign tests and the ASN1_LONG_UNDEF/zero sentinels match, and every refusal raises the authority's coordinate.

mechanisms: X509_PKEY repr(C) layout and offset assertions
RawCtx publication window before both members exist
CtxDestroy member body and key_free gate
file_dispositions.note: The raw window releases only the block if allocation fails; the two members are written before assume_init; the failure path drops the partially built value (members then block) and raises X509_PKEY_28. Member release order, EVP_PKEY_free and the key_free test match x_pkey.c.

defects.kind: unsafe contract understated the allocation extent of a UINT32 value
defects.detail: uint32_free's SAFETY comment said the slot always held the four-byte block uint32_new installs, but uint32_c2i deliberately allocates through uint64_new (eight bytes), as the authority does. OwnedBlock's Drop releases the allocation base pointer and never uses the typed extent, so the release was already whole and no UB or leak existed; the false statement is now corrected to name both provenances and the extent-independent release.

defects.kind: unsafe contract omitted mandatory template fields the body dereferences
defects.detail: The # Safety contract named only spkac, while NETSCAPE_SPKI_print reads spkac->pubkey, spkac->challenge, sig_algor.algorithm and signature. A valid item value always has them (ASN1_SIMPLE/ASN1_EMBED templates), but the stated contract did not establish it. The contract now names all five. No code change; the authority dereferences the same fields.

secret_buffers.cleansed_on: bn_free's BN_clear_free when the item size carries BN_SENSITIVE
secret_buffers.released_on: the same BN_clear_free (BN_SENSITIVE is read from the item, not the algorithm)
secret_buffers.note: The secure-heap allocation and BN_FLG_CONSTTIME stamp are preserved; the clear-free arm is never replaced by BN_free for a sensitive item.

secret_buffers.cleansed_on: OwnedBuf's Drop over the full allocation length on every exit, including a failed BIO_printf
secret_buffers.note: The authority uses OPENSSL_clear_free(buf, buflen); the owner keeps both the allocation length and the cleansing release.

secret_buffers.cleansed_on: EVP_PKEY_free's own key-type destructor (not a local copy)
secret_buffers.note: The record owns the pointer and releases it exactly once in the authority's order.

secret_buffers.released_on: CRYPTO_free at x_pkey.c:44 when key_free is set
secret_buffers.note: The legacy PEM record's encrypted-key scratch; the authority releases it plainly and only when key_free is set.

secret_buffers.buffer: NETSCAPE_SPKI challenge, signature and public key
secret_buffers.released_on: caller-owned item values; the temporary EVP_PKEY from X509_PUBKEY_get is freed here
secret_buffers.note: The only owned temporary on this path is the EVP_PKEY, released once after printing.
